paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Real love for God's people costs something, and it gives gladly. Paul says, "And for the sake of your souls, I will most gladly spend my money and myself." (2 Corinthians 12:15) He wasn't after their stuff. He says, "I am not seeking your possessions, but you." (2 Corinthians 12:14)

Now look at WHY he's saying all this. Paul asks, "Have you been thinking all along that we were making a defense to you?" Then he tells them, "We speak before God in Christ, and all of this, beloved, is to build you up." (2 Corinthians 12:19) I think that's the heart of it: a good teacher isn't there to win the argument, he's there to build you up, and he does it in front of God.

And that's why he gets so honest about his fears. He's afraid of finding quarreling, jealousy, gossip and more, and he's afraid he'll be grieved over many who "have not repented." (2 Corinthians 12:20-21) Friend, that's what love looks like when it's not pretending everything is fine. So when God's Word gets honest with you, take it as someone caring enough to build you up, and let it do its work.
